title: Zion’s redemption requires volunteers, means, and obedience
setting: Two Missouri leaders, Parley Pratt and Lyman Wight, arrived in Kirtland on 24 February 1834. They reported to the Kirtland high council on the exiled Saints, most of them in Clay County. They asked how Zion would be redeemed. At that meeting Joseph Smith offered to lead an expedition, and thirty or forty others volunteered. Joseph dictated this revelation the same day, but records do not show whether before, during, or after the meeting.
summary: The revelation tells the Lord’s “friends” how to act for their scattered brethren in Zion. It says the Saints were chastened because they did not fully obey. If they now hearken, they will begin to prevail. If not, the world will prevail against them. The scattered will return and build up Zion, but only if they do not pollute their inheritances. Zion’s redemption must come by power, led by a man like Moses. Joseph Smith is named as the servant in the earlier parable of the vineyard. He is to gather the young and middle-aged men to Zion. Pairs of recruiters are sent out to seek five hundred men, and no fewer than one hundred.

contextNote.title: Redemption tied to hearkening
contextNote.text: The exiles wanted to know how they could return to Jackson County. Verse 15 says Zion’s redemption must come by power. Verses 5–8 first set the condition: the Saints will prevail only if they hearken from that very hour. Verse 14 adds that even restored lands can be lost if they are polluted. Verses 31–34 show the same pattern in recruiting, asking for five hundred but allowing fewer. In this passage, power to redeem Zion is promised, but always on condition of obedience.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 102–105, “After Much Tribulation … Cometh the Blessing,” draws from verse 12 that blessings can follow trials. What conditions do verses 5–8 and 36 attach to the promised victory, and how might they apply to a blessing you are seeking?
reviewNote: Read all 40 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, 24 February 1834, after Pratt and Wight arrived from Missouri. JSP historical introduction read for the high council meeting, Joseph’s offer to lead, the uncertain order of revelation and meeting, the recruiters, and the resulting Camp of Israel (Zion’s Camp) of about 205 men. Verses 24–26 speak of cursing and avenging enemies; the summary follows the text without comment. Liberty used to represent Clay County.
